context.body: Then David came to Nob to Ahimelech the priest. Ahimelech came to meet David trembling, and said to him, “Why are you alone, and no man with you?”.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: David comes alone to Ahimelech, gives a mission account, receives consecrated bread, and asks for the sword kept behind the ephod.
observations.label: Holy bread and Goliath’s sword: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps David, Ahimelech, the young men, and Doeg, Nob and the sanctuary, concealing, questioning, giving bread, observing purity, and retrieving a sword visible within David's story or later memory.
observations.label: Holy bread and Goliath’s sword: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: David, Ahimelech, the young men, and Doeg · Nob and the sanctuary · concealing, questioning, giving bread, observing purity, and retrieving a sword · flight acquires food, a weapon, and a dangerous witness
observations.label: Relationships named in 1 Samuel 21:1–9

payload.posture: Read 1 Samuel 21:1–9 as its own flight, covenant, and restraint David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places flight acquires food, a weapon, and a dangerous witness inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
payload.title: Holy bread and Goliath’s sword
